blocks.x: "How much will it cost?" is the first question on most commercial projects, and the hardest to answer from a phone call. No reliable commercial renovation cost per square foot in Winnipeg exists without seeing the space, so this guide gives no dollar figure.

Two spaces of the same size can cost very different amounts depending on what's behind the walls and what the space needs to do. Here's what drives the cost of a commercial renovation in Winnipeg, and how to get a number you can trust.

Commercial renovation cost per square foot by project type
No per-square-foot figures here, only a rough general order from lower to higher, not published data. Any one project can break it:
**Cosmetic refresh:** paint, flooring, lighting, ceiling tiles
**Office fit-out:** new walls, meeting rooms, finishes, some electrical and HVAC
**Retail fit-out:** storefront, display, lighting, washroom
**Medical or dental clinic:** exam rooms, sinks, specialized plumbing and ventilation
**Restaurant:** commercial kitchen, grease interceptor, exhaust hood, fire suppression
Hidden costs to plan for
**Asbestos testing and abatement** in older Winnipeg buildings before demolition
**Code upgrades** triggered by the renovation (accessibility, fire separations, exits)
**Electrical service upgrades** for equipment-heavy uses
**After-hours premiums** if you can't close during work

**Contingency:** [set aside a contingency fund](https://www.bdc.ca/en/articles-tools/money-finance/buy-lease-commercial-real-estate/how-to-protect-your-business-when-making-lease-hold-improvements) for surprises, and a larger one in older buildings
How to get an accurate quote
**Bring a clear brief:** how many people, what rooms, what equipment, what hours you need to stay open.
**Share any drawings or photos** of the existing space.
**Ask for a site visit,** not just a phone estimate.
**Compare line items,** not just totals. Check what's an allowance vs. a firm price.
**Ask what's excluded:** design, permits, furniture, IT and signage are often separate.
Ways to control cost
Reuse existing walls, ceilings and mechanical where possible
Choose durable mid-range finishes over premium ones
Keep plumbing fixtures near existing lines
Decide early and avoid mid-project changes
The bottom line
The cost of a commercial renovation depends far more on use, systems and existing conditions than on square footage alone. A site visit and a detailed scope are the only way to a reliable number.
